title: Dashboard surface manifest: mini kit for ops & cost-aware panels
content:
Goal:
Provide a compact, operator-friendly manifest that defines the minimal dashboard surface area operators need for token-serving inference stacks. Focus: low-cardinality, high-signal panels that are cheap to query and fast to interpret during incidents.

Audience:
- Oncall SREs and Operators
- Eng product owners rolling out model variants
- Observability engineers who author panels and sampling policies

Why a mini kit?
- Full observability decks are expensive to maintain and cost money per query.
- During incidents we want a 5-panel view that answers the triage questions quickly (Isolate, Impact, Cause, Remediate).
- This doc defines which panels, exact metric definitions, trace anchors, sampling guidance, and query-cost estimates for each.

Manifest: 5-panel minimal surface (panels ordered by triage priority)
1) Incoming request rate + 95/99 latency rollup (global)
   - Metric name(s): requests.count, inference.latency_ms{quantile="p95"}, inference.latency_ms{quantile="p99"}
   - Definition: requests.count = number of inference API calls (post-auth). Latency quantiles computed at 1m aggregation with N=100 sample min.
   - Why: Detect throughput spikes and tail latency.
   - Query cost note: pre-aggregated (counter + summary) - estimated 0.2 query-units/1m panel.

2) Error surface: top error buckets by classification (4 bars)
   - Metric name(s): inference.errors{type}, http_errors.count{status_class}
   - Definition: Group by error.type (model_timeout, kv_miss, kernel_error, rate_limited). Include 5xx and 4xx bucket counts.
   - Display: stacked bar for last 5m and table root-cause links.
   - Trace anchor label: attach trace ids for any error.type != "model_timeout" when count>5 in 1m.

3) Cold-cache/kv-warmth index (tenant-weighted)
   - Metric name(s): kv.cache_hit_ratio, kv.prefetch_warmth_index
   - Definition: kv.cache_hit_ratio = hits / (hits+misses) per tenant over 5m. Warmth index = fraction of requests that benefited from prefix/KV cache. For multi-tenant, show top-5 tenants by request rate.
   - Why: Cold cache often explains sudden latency regressions.
   - Sampling: instrument exponential decay per-tenant to avoid spike noise.

4) Slow-path breakdown (operator-friendly waterfall)
   - Metric name(s): runtime.decode_ms, runtime.attention_ms, runtime.kv_lookup_ms, runtime.kernel_ms, network.rtt_ms
   - Definition: per-request histogram; panel shows median + p75/p95 for each span category. Waterfall constructed by summing span medians for typical sessions.
   - Trace anchors: include one representative trace per quantile (p50/p95) with span ids and brief span durations.

5) Cost & throughput amortization (tokens/min & GPU utilization)
   - Metric name(s): token_count.total, gpu.utilization, batch_efficiency
   - Definition: tokens/min measured at service ingress; batch_efficiency = average effective batch size / configured batch target. GPU utilization from node exporter or exporter proxy.
   - Why: tie economic signal to ops — when utilization low & tokens high, batching misconfig.
   - Query cost note: heavy (joins across exporters) — schedule 1/min scrape, panel cache at 1m.

Panel sizing & query-budget heuristics
- Use coarse-grained panels (1m resolution) for rollup charts; 10s resolution only for synthetic probes.
- Avoid per-tenant high-cardinality panels on default oncall view; put per-tenant explorables as 2-click drilldowns.
- Budget: keep default dashboard query cost <= 2 query-units/min for oncall environment. Flag heavy panels for weekday/weekday-hours only.

Metric definitions (authoritative forms)
- requests.count: "sum(rate(api.request_total[1m])) by (service, env)"
- inference.latency_ms.histogram: exported from runtime as hdr histogram; compute p95/p99 via histogram_quantile(0.95/0.99, sum(rate(runtime_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le))
- kv.cache_hit_ratio: "sum(kv_hits[5m]) / (sum(kv_hits[5m]) + sum(kv_misses[5m])) by (tenant)" (use safe denominator codepath to avoid div by zero)

Trace sampling & annotation rules (compact)
- Sampling budget: 1 trace / 1000 requests baseline, increased to 1/100 during anomalies (error rate > 0.5% or p99 latency > SLO).
- Priority sampling for: errors, slow-path p99, batch size below threshold, KV miss on cold-start events.
- Annotate traces with: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), model_variant, batch_size, kv_warmth_flag, route_policy. These make triage faster without exposing PII.

Operator quick-actions (to include as buttons on panel)
- Drain node: /runbook/drain-node (link to playbook)
- Toggle fallback model: feature flag endpoint with audit link
- Increase sampling: toggle sampler to 1/100 for 15m windows

Ownership & lifecycle notes
- Panel owner: eng-observability (rotation: Aisha, Mateo, Priya) — keep note of who edited last and reason (release, incident, experiment).
- Review cadence: triage after any model rollout > 10% traffic or change to batching config. Quarterly review for deprecated panels.

Templates & snippet library (for dashboard authors)
- Compact latency panel snippet: "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le, service))"
- Error-class table: "topk(5, sum(rate(inference_errors_total[5m])) by (error_type))"
- KV warmth: use rolling window with min_samples threshold: "(sum(kv_hits[5m]) + 1) / (sum(kv_hits[5m]) + sum(kv_misses[5m]) + 1)"

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- How to encode tenant-weighted SLOs in single panel without exploding cardinality? (options: quantile-by-tenant, sampling, pivot to top-k only)
- Should we add a compact ML-quality signal (RLHF drift) to the mini kit? pros/cons re: label latency and query cost.
- Confirm read-only RBAC for the default oncall dashboard (prevent accidental heavy queries).

References & links
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OBS-7841 (dashboard governance)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/456 (hdr histogram export changes)
- Slack threads: #obs-ops for operational playbook updates (see pinned messages Feb 2025)

Appendix: short incident playflow mapped to panels
1) Operator sees p99 spike on panel 1 -> open panel 4 (waterfall) to identify slow span
2) If span = kv_miss -> check panel 3 (kv warmth) and search traces for recent cold-cache events
3) If span = kernel_error or attention_ms -> check panel 2 for correlated errors and escalate to runtime oncall
4) Toggle sampler via panel button and attach representative traces to JIRA ticket for postmortem

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact; want feedback on whether 5 panels feels sufficient for first-response. If approval, next steps: produce Grafana JSON + playbook links and trial in next oncall rotation.
